doc.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022

title: Missing studio spaces and recording Air Force bands
summary: He misses the many New York studios and recalls recording Air Force bands in Anchorage, Dallas and Omaha, and big band sessions.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Is there anything that you miss, a bygone technology, the tape or those massive plate reverbs or something like that?

I just — what I miss is that a lot of the nice studio spaces here in New York and also in general have all gone away. The need for that and having all of these musicians play together is few and far between. That is I used to do a bunch of work for Air Force bands and go to different studios. I went to a studio in Anchorage, Alaska to record different bands and Anchorage in the middle of January is a real garden spot let me tell ya. And I did work in Dallas and in Omaha with these bands. And to first of all go in and do that and set things up and you know you walk into a studio and it’s like well let’s see you’ve got a coffee maker and you’ve got a couple of condenser mics, oh and you have a pencil
